Verifying a flight booking is essential — it prevents costly mistakes, reduces travel stress, and ensures you meet entry and airline requirements. Below are key reasons, practical steps, and a short checklist your traveler can use to confirm their booking with confidence.

Why verification matters
- Prevents errors (wrong name spelling, date, airport, class) that can be hard or costly to fix.
- Ensures payment actually went through and the ticket is ticketed (not just a hold).
- Confirms compliance with entry rules (passport validity, visas, vaccinations), avoiding denied boarding.
- Lets you catch changes or schedule disruptions early so you can rebook or claim refunds.

What to verify (high priority)
- Passenger name(s) exactly as on passport/ID.
- Travel date and time (departure and arrival).
- Departure and arrival airports (e.g., LAX → HND or NRT).
- Flight number(s) and airline(s).
- Cabin class and seat assignment (business class confirmed).
- Booking reference / e‑ticket number.
- Payment status and the last 4 digits of the card used (do not share full card/CVV in chat).
- Baggage allowance and fees.
- Cancellation / change policy and any travel insurance coverage.
- Contact phone and email on the booking (for updates).
- Passport expiration date and visa requirements for the destination.
- Any special requests (meals, wheelchair, pets).

When to verify (recommended timeline)
- Immediately after booking: confirm booking reference, e‑ticket, payment, and name spelling.
- 48–72 hours after booking: re-check airline website or booking status to ensure ticket is confirmed.
- 7–14 days before travel: confirm schedules and seat assignments; check visa/entry rules.
- 24–48 hours before departure: check-in online and reconfirm terminal/gate and baggage rules.
- Day of travel: check flight status for delays or cancellations.

How to verify (practical methods)
- Check the confirmation email for booking reference and e‑ticket. Save or screenshot it.
- Log in directly on the airline’s website (use booking ref + last name) to view/ticket and manage booking.
- Use the airline app to store boarding passes and receive push alerts.
- Call the airline or travel agency if anything looks wrong or if you never received an e‑ticket.
- Compare the card statement to ensure the charge matches the booking amount.
- Add booking details to a secure travel folder (digital or printed) and your calendar with reminders.
- Take screenshots of confirmations but avoid storing CVV or full card numbers.

If you find a discrepancy
- Contact the airline or agency immediately (phone is fastest for urgent errors).
- Provide booking reference and describe the discrepancy (name, date, airport, payment).
- Keep evidence: confirmation emails, payment receipts, and screenshots.
- If the airline won’t resolve it, document the interaction (names, timestamps) and escalate via the agency’s or airline’s support channels.

Security & privacy reminders
- Never share full card numbers or CVV in chat/email. Share only the last 4 digits if needed for verification.
- Use official airline websites or trusted booking portals to log in and view tickets.
- Keep travel documents and copies secure (password manager, encrypted storage, or physical safe).

- [ ] Booking reference & e‑ticket present
- [ ] Passenger name(s) match passport
- [ ] Dates/times correct
- [ ] Airports confirmed (departure/arrival)
- [ ] Flight number & airline match

- [ ] Screenshots/records saved securely
